claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch on a compliant basis because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, monitored rollout controls are in place, and the known developer-support migration limitation will be handled through mandatory model-card disclosure rather than treated as eliminated by rollout controls.
specific_concerns: The actor summary says the affected developer-support migration segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The current risk-acceptance draft is described as unapproved and not covering the exposed segment.
The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
No admissible evidence is provided that the required model-card disclosure has actually been completed before certification.
The recommendation to certify appears to depend on a condition being satisfied, but the record provided does not show that condition has been met.
unsupported_claims: Any unconditional claim that certification is already compliant on the present record.
Any claim that a 7% rollout, rollback switch, or monitoring can substitute for the required disclosure while the affected use case remains exposed.
Any claim that risk acceptance presently cures the disclosure problem.
evidence_requests: Provide the final pre-launch model card or equivalent approved disclosure artifact showing the developer-support migration limitation is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Provide approval records or publication evidence confirming that disclosure was completed before launch/certification.
If relying on risk acceptance instead of disclosure, provide the reviewed and approved risk-acceptance document that explicitly covers the developer-support migration exposure.
Provide the exact certification decision language to confirm whether certification was conditional on disclosure or issued unconditionally.
decision_criteria: If the exposed use case remains in scope, certification is compliant only if the material limitation is disclosed before launch or an approved risk acceptance explicitly covers that exposure.
Aggregate readiness clearance and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch readiness, but they do not by themselves satisfy the model-card disclosure requirement.
Rollout controls and monitoring count only as supplemental mitigation unless they exclude the affected use case or are paired with approved risk acceptance.
A compliant certification record must be supportable from admissible evidence, not from conditional or aspirational wording alone.
